content.title: Capital To Country Multi Day Ultra 2026
content.text: OverviewThe 4th edition of the Capital to Country Multi Day Ultra is a challenging and immersive five-day, self-sufficient trail stage race set in the rugged hills and rural landscapes east of Kathmandu, Nepal. Covering approximately 197 km (around 123 miles), the event offers a rare blend of demanding mountain running and deep cultural immersion, taking runners through remote villages, forested ridgelines, jeep tracks, and traditional trails rarely seen by visitors.The race begins near the Kathmandu Valley, including a ceremonial start at the iconic Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), before heading steadily into quieter, more rural terrain. Designed for experienced trail and ultra runners, the event combines physical challenge with meaningful interaction with local communities, making it as much a journey as a race.Route & Daily StagesThe course is divided into five stages, each with its own character and challenges. While exact routes may vary slightly year to year, the overall structure and difficulty remain consistent.Approximate stage breakdown:Stage 1: Sankhu to Kasibanjayang – ~43 kmStage 2: Kasibanjayang to Bhakundebesi – ~40 kmStage 3: Bhakundebesi to Mukpatar – ~43 kmStage 4: Mukpatar to Lama Home – ~38 kmStage 5: Lama Trail Marathon – ~43 kmTotal distance: ~197 kmTotal elevation change: approximately 10,000 m of ascent and descentRunners can expect steep climbs, long runnable sections, technical descents, and frequent changes in terrain. Daily elevation gain is significant, demanding strong climbing fitness and careful pacing.Challenge & FormatThe race is primarily self-sufficient, meaning runners carry their own food, mandatory equipment, and personal supplies. A lighter-load option is available, where organisers transport food and sleeping equipment between stages.Accommodation during the race is provided in pre-arranged campsites and village bunkhouses, allowing participants to experience rural Nepal firsthand. One highlight of the event is a traditional monk blessing before the final stage.This event is best suited to runners with:Prior ultra-distance or stage-race experienceComfort running long distances on mountainous terrainExperience managing kit, nutrition, and recovery over multiple daysDates & LogisticsNext scheduled edition: November 2026Arrival: Kathmandu by 22 November for registration, briefing, and kit checksRace duration: 5 race days, plus arrival and departure logisticsThe race includes transfers, accommodation before and after the event, and full on-course organisation.Entry Cost & Payment ScheduleTotal entry fee: approximately £1,775Payment structure:£375 – non-refundable deposit at registration£450 – due by 31 July£475 – due by 31 August£475 – due by 30 SeptemberPlaces are limited (typically around 20 runners), and early registration is advised.What’s IncludedAirport and race transfersHotel accommodation before and after the raceCampsite or village accommodation during the raceWater, basic camp services, and local support crewsGPS tracking and event organisationNot included: international flights, Nepal visa, insurance, personal equipment, and food (unless using the lighter-load option).Why Enter?The Capital to Country Multi Day Ultra is ideal for runners seeking a true adventure race — one that goes beyond medals and finish times. It offers demanding mountain running, cultural authenticity, and a strong sense of camaraderie among participants, all set against the dramatic backdrop of Nepal’s Himalayan foothills.Useful LinksOfficial race page:https://www.gobeyondchallenge.com/ultra-marathons/capital-to-country-multi-day-ultra/Event listing and background information:https://trailrunningnepal.org/trail-races/nepal-multi-day-ultra-2025/Registration platform:https://gobeyondevents.eventrac.co.uk
